what_it_does: Wearable devices like smartwatches often harvest their own energy from the environment — from body heat, movement, or light — but that energy supply is unpredictable and varies from moment to moment. If a device uses too much energy when little is coming in, its battery dies; if it is too conservative, it misses opportunities to run useful tasks. This paper builds a system that predicts future energy availability not as a single number but as a range of likely values, using a technique called conformal prediction that comes with a mathematical guarantee that the true value will fall inside the predicted range a specified percentage of the time. The device then simulates many possible energy futures by drawing samples from that range (a Monte Carlo approach) and uses a small, fast machine-learning model to pick the best action given all those possible futures, enabling smarter and safer energy decisions.
